It depends on what marker of inflammation you are using. C-Reactive Protein is probably the most common blood marker used to assess cardiovascular inflammation as it is associated with atherosclerotic events (cardiovascular disease) and with elevated blood lipids (LDL). You can basically assume that most people with elevated LDL also have higher CRP.

Inflammation in the skin for example may involve a different set of markers than in the arteries, and some markers will be shared. Certain prostaglandings and eicosanoids in the gut will be elevated in response to a food sensitivity that you wouldn't use as markers for inflammation elsewhere.

My best friend from college was a total foil to my own personality. We loved the same things, hated the same things, had our own individual issues with family. But after college was over, he was almost a brother to me. He showed me how to rebel against my parents a bit, I never crossed the line too much, save for smoking some weed and having a party. For me, these were big departures.

Things changed when I found out he was severely in debt after flunking out of his accounting major. His Dad forced him to go to work to get started chipping away at his college debt. He started a construction job, but was forced into the union, who kept on giving him the run around and pushing him to stay in when they were taking chunks of money out of his paycheck for absolutely doing nothing. He became really depressed. Despite this, he didn't share what he was going through with anyone.

He committed suicide when he was 21. I was 22. It was a shock to everyone. He went missing for one weekend after lying to his family about taking a trip north to see his grandparents. When they couldn't find him, they hired an investigator, who found him when they discovered an unclaimed body found not far away from where he had parked the car and left his belongings. He used a Ruger .380 and one shot to the temple. I'll never forget his funeral, I sent flowers, and his Dad asked me to be a pallbearer.

They found about 8 empty cough syrup bottles in his car, and about 3 in his room, hidden in his belongings. He had been abusing cough syrup for months prior to this event. No one even saw anything out of the ordinary. A lot of his family questioned if they could have helped him more if they paid attention, but I don't think it was their fault or mine. I don't think he wanted to survive anymore, because he couldn't see a future for himself where he was capable at all of being happy. That's the worst part of being young, depression hits you 10x harder because you don't have enough positive things to compare it with. There are a lot of positive things that you can't see because you take them for granted.

It's cathartic to talk about things like this here. I'm so sorry for your family, from the bottom of my heart. We all have reasons to carry on, just find the one thing about him that made you the happiest and continue it as a tradition in their honor. My friend loved the Big Lebowski, I watch it every year on the anniversary of his birthday, which is actually the first time I ever watched that movie. It means something else to me now.
